name: Dev Team
description: The software-engineering agent team, shipped as one installable unit: the Coder family (Sonnet / Opus / Haiku / GPT5) that writes the code, the Product Owner that decides what is worth building, the Architect that decides how it should be shaped, the skills defining each contract, and the Software Engineering Agents Flow that says how they hand off to one another. Every agent runs on the same config the workspace's existing coder agents use.

skills.description: Contract for the Product Owner agent — owns what gets built and why, turns a vague ask into a scoped, testable outcome, and stays out of how it is implemented. Says no, and says it early.

Contract for the Architect agent — decides how a change should be shaped against the codebase that already exists, writes the decision down with its trade-offs, and hands the coders a plan grounded in real file paths rather than a sketch.

agent_configs.name: Dev Team
agent_configs.description: The same bundle the workspace's existing coder agents run under (agent-config-aw-full), declared here so a fresh workspace gets it without anyone recreating it by hand: full workspace filesystem access, the shared network, git/GitHub and docker, /tmp, and the aw-gateway MCP server — without which there is no knowledge base to check a design against and no Kanban to file the work into.

groups.name: Dev Team
groups.description: Product Owner, Architect and the Coder family — the agents that take a request from 'somebody wants this' to 'this is merged'.
groups.capabilities: Scopes, designs, implements and verifies changes to a real codebase. Reads the knowledge base before deciding anything, works against the repo the run's cwd points at, and reports what actually changed.

groups.name: Coders
groups.description: The build lane — the Coder family across models (Sonnet / Opus / Haiku / GPT-5), same contract, chosen by what the task is worth.
groups.capabilities: Generic coding specialists — read code before changing it, implement a scoped feature, fix or refactor end to end in the repo the run targets, and verify it before reporting. Hand off any 'write or fix code' task here.

groups.name: QAs
groups.description: QA Engineers — the review lane. Same Dev Team rules, but they decide whether what came out is what was asked for, and they never fix it themselves.
groups.capabilities: QA reviewers — validate a finished Kanban task's delivery against its requirements and decide the card's next status (done / ready to deploy / need human). Hand off review and verification tasks here — never implementation.

agents.name: Coder - Sonnet
agents.description: The default coder. Reads code, writes code, runs it, reports what changed. Pick this one unless the task specifically wants a cheaper or a deeper model.
agents.capabilities: Implements a scoped coding task end to end in the repo this run targets — bug fix, feature, refactor or investigation — and verifies it before reporting.
use_cases: implement this feature
fix this bug
refactor this module
why does this test fail

agents.name: Coder - Opus
agents.description: The coder for work where getting it wrong is expensive — a change that spans subsystems, a bug nobody has been able to reproduce, a refactor with no test coverage to catch a mistake.
agents.capabilities: Same contract as Coder - Sonnet, on the deepest model. For tasks where a wrong answer costs more than the extra tokens.
use_cases: this bug has survived two fix attempts
change that spans several subsystems
refactor code with no tests to catch a mistake

agents.name: Coder - Haiku
agents.description: The coder for mechanical work — a rename across many files, a lint sweep, a dependency bump. Cheap and fast; hand it tasks where the answer is already decided.
agents.capabilities: Same contract as Coder - Sonnet, on the cheapest model. For high-volume, low-judgement edits.
use_cases: rename this symbol everywhere
apply this same edit across 30 files
bump the dependency and fix the fallout

agents.name: Coder - GPT5
agents.description: The coder on a different vendor's model, via the Codex CLI. Useful as a second opinion when a Claude-backed coder has stalled on something, and as the fallback when Anthropic is degraded.
agents.capabilities: Same contract as Coder - Sonnet, running the Codex CLI on GPT-5 — a genuinely independent implementation attempt, not the same model retried.
use_cases: get a second opinion from a different model
the Claude coders keep converging on the same wrong fix
Anthropic is down and this still needs shipping

agents.name: Product Owner
agents.description: Owns what gets built and why. Turns a vague ask into a scoped outcome with a stated user, a stated success condition and an explicit out-of-scope list — and says no to the work that shouldn't happen, before anyone writes code for it.
agents.capabilities: Scopes a request into something buildable and verifiable: who it's for, what changes for them, how we'll know it worked, what is deliberately not in it. Decides priority and trade-offs. Does not decide implementation.
use_cases: somebody asked for X — is it worth building, and what exactly is it
cut this scope down to something shippable this week
write acceptance criteria for this request
should we do this now or later

agents.name: UX Coder - Sonnet
agents.description: Owns a prototype end to end, with a mandate for usability rather than for the literal ask: thinks past the request to what the user will actually try next, and makes sure that path exists and works. UX craft calls are its own; genuine product decisions go back to the Product Owner.
agents.capabilities: Builds and iterates a working prototype, judging it by whether someone could pick it up and use it without hitting a wall — not by whether it matches the sentence that was asked for.
use_cases: build a prototype for this idea
this screen is confusing — make it usable
iterate on the prototype with this feedback

agents.name: QA - Sonnet
agents.description: Validates a finished delivery against what was actually asked for and decides the outcome — never writes the feature itself. The default QA: reach for it when the review needs judgement about whether the thing genuinely works.
agents.capabilities: Reviews a completed task: checks the delivery against the request, verifies it rather than taking the report's word for it, and records a verdict — moving the Kanban card when there is one.
use_cases: review what the coder just delivered
does this actually do what the card asked for
is this ready to deploy or does it need another pass

agents.name: QA - Haiku
agents.description: The cheap QA pass, for deliveries where the check is mechanical — the file exists, the test runs, the command exits zero. Escalate to QA - Sonnet when the verdict turns on judgement rather than on a fact.
agents.capabilities: Same contract as QA - Sonnet, on the cheapest model. For high-volume, low-judgement verification.
use_cases: quick check that this delivery is what it says
verify the build passes and the files landed
cheap first-pass review before a human looks

agents.name: Architect
agents.description: Decides how a change should be shaped against the codebase that already exists — which seam it goes through, what it must not break, what it makes harder later — and writes the decision down with its trade-offs so the coders inherit a plan, not a sketch.
agents.capabilities: Turns a scoped requirement into a design grounded in the real code: the seam to change, the files involved, the alternatives rejected and why, and the risks a coder should watch for. Reads far more than it writes.
use_cases: how should we build this
which of these two designs should we pick
will this change break anything we can't see
review this plan before we start coding

agents.name: Debugger
agents.description: Finds out why before anybody changes anything — states a falsifiable hypothesis, runs the smallest experiment that could kill it, and reports a root cause with the evidence. Diagnoses; hands the fix to a Coder.
agents.capabilities: Diagnoses a symptom to its root cause in the real code — failing test, wrong output, crash, works-here-not-there — and reports the evidence plus a proposed fix for a coder to implement.
use_cases: why does this test fail
this crashes and I don't know why
find the root cause of this bug
it works locally but not in the container

agents.name: Doc Writer
agents.description: Writes up what the team built — README, ADR, module docs, API reference — grounded in the code as it actually is. The one role whose finished work completes straight to Done instead of going through QA.
agents.capabilities: Produces documentation for an existing change or module, read from the code rather than from the request — README, ADR, module docs, API reference.
use_cases: document what we just built
write a README for this module
write an ADR for this decision
document this API

agent_flows.name: Agents Flow: Software Engineering
agent_flows.description: How a request becomes shipped code: it arrives at Source, the Product Owner decides what it actually is and whether it's worth doing, the Architect decides how it should be shaped, and the Coder family implements it. UX Coder hangs off Source and the PO directly — that placement is not a preference, it is what aw-agent-ux-coder already tells that agent about itself. Every edge is two-way: a design that turns out to be expensive is a scope conversation, and a coder with a genuine product question routes it back to the PO instead of guessing. The QAs group closes the loop: every builder edges into it, and because adjacency is two-way a rejected delivery routes straight back to whoever built it — which is what lets QA review without ever fixing. That placement is documented in aw-agent-qa, the skill those agents actually read; the graph is the bug if the two disagree.

apps.reason: Provides the contributes.agents surface — it holds the Agents Platform base URL and identity token, which core does not. The floor matters twice over: 0.55.0 is the first version that can seed an agent_flows entry at all (older ones create the six agents and silently drop the flow, leaving a team with no topology), and it is also the app that ships the aw-agent-coder skill every Coder here references by slug. Non-required on purpose: a declaration that arrives before the provider is HELD and replayed the moment one appears, so this app installs cleanly either way.

Supplies search_knowledge_base, which all three contracts make a mandatory first step. Non-required, but the team is materially worse without it: the KB is what stops the Architect re-deciding something already decided and the PO re-scoping something already shipped.
